Fixes bug Bc99060b8ca: claim refuses an item whose lease is past its expiry (for another -76s) and only reports waiting; claim --force is not an option, release --force is

Write the regression test first and watch it FAIL on the unfixed code; then `ddflow complete fix-Bc99060b8ca --regression-test <test>` closes the bug with the task (or `ddflow bug fixed Bc99060b8ca --regression-test <test>` first).
data.title: Fix bug Bc99060b8ca: claim on an expired lease still refuses

chunk_findings.detail: `health_lines` is the single funnel this change wires into the surfaces: `overview.py` uses it for `data["health"]`, and `wait_order` appends it to the doctor `notes`. Its filter unconditionally discards every finding whose `kind` is `H.CRASHED` (and every finding whose `evidence["via"] == "cycle"`), so the fastest crash signal the watchdog produces never reaches any of these surfaces. Concrete input: a lane holding a live, being-renewed lease whose heartbeat reports a pid/host/session that no longer exist (or is being renewed by a straggling heartbeat loop, the 2026-10-15 "stopped agent" case). `HW.inspect` returns a finding of kind `H.CRASHED`; `health_lines` drops it because `f.kind != H.CRASHED` is False, so `data["health"]` in the status/overview payload and the doctor notes are empty for that lane, and the brief/statusline/dispatcher-plan consumers built on them see nothing — even though the stated intent makes CRASHED ("the holder's process or session is gone ... so a dead process is seen in minutes, not after the 30-minute TTL") a required inspected condition with a correction step ("take over or relaunch from the worktree"). The docstring's justification, "Finding lines not already shown elsewhere", does not hold for this case: the only other lease-related surface (`recoverable`) covers the lease-expired-with-work case, not a dead pid behind a still-valid lease, so a crashed lane stays invisible until the TTL lapses, which is exactly the detection latency this change is supposed to remove.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/reporting/waitcycles.py:health_lines (the `f.kind != H.CRASHED` filter, ~line 57)

chunk_findings.detail: The section only exposes limits for two of the conditions the watchdog must detect: `stall_s` (STALLED) and `runaway_s` (RUNAWAY). The change's own specification names three further required knobs — `[watch].idle_s` for IDLE-HEARTBEAT ("renewals continue but nothing else for [watch].idle_s"), `[watch].reply_s` for UNRESPONSIVE ("a nudge or yield request went unanswered for [watch].reply_s") and `[watch].crash_s` for CRASHED ("a dead pid is CRASHED within [watch].crash_s ... seen in minutes, not after the 30-minute TTL") — and its CONFORMANCE clause requires "every limit, mode and interval a knob settable by file, CLI, MCP and prompt, per project and org" [r-everything-configurable]. With this section as written, an operator can set how long a *lease-renewing* lane may make no progress (`stall_s`) but cannot set the dead-pid/session-gone detection window, the idle-heartbeat window, or the nudge-reply window: those can only be hard-coded, so the very "seen in minutes" behaviour the operator asked for is not configurable (e.g. setting `[health].crash_s = 120` has no field to bind to and is silently ignored / rejected, and the watchdog cannot be tuned faster than its built-in threshold). The class docstring even claims it covers "stalled, locked, crashed and runaway lanes" while crash has no knob at all.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/config_sections/health.py:12-42 (HealthConfig knobs)

chunk_findings.detail: `mode` is a single string applied to every finding kind, but the specification requires the correction mode to be settable *per finding kind* ("a mode per step ([watch].act = off | advise | act, default advise, per finding kind)"): an operator must be able to, say, leave lock/cycle findings at `propose` while letting a CRASHED lane's lease be expired in `apply`, or run `apply` for runaways only. With one global field, `[health].mode = "apply"` turns on lease-breaking and `needs`-edge insertion for *all* kinds at once, so there is no configuration under which the documented ladder is applied selectively as specified; a project that wants detection-and-report for deadlocks but automatic recovery for crashes cannot express it.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/config_sections/health.py:15-21 (HealthConfig.mode)

chunk_findings.detail: `recorded` is computed as `not lz.live(lz.renewed_at)`. A lease is always live at its own renewal instant (`renewed_at < renewed_at + ttl [+ grace]`), so this expression is `False` for every lane, live or expired, regardless of what the log holds. The comment says "an expiry is recorded, whatever the clock says", but the value never consults the log at all — even though the record that actually answers the question is already sitting right there in `rec` (`recs.get(i)`, line 85, keyed on `kind == "expired_lease"`). Concretely: take a lane whose process died leaving work, whose lease has expired and for which `L.scan` already yields an `expired_lease` record (so `rec is not None`, `work is True`). `gather` still hands `H.Lane(..., work=True, recorded=False, ...)`, so `correct`'s guard `f.evidence.get("work") is True and not f.evidence["recorded"]` (line ~163) is always satisfied. In `apply` mode `L.expire` is therefore re-invoked for an already-expired lane on every watchdog pass, and in `propose` mode a "would record ... expired" line is emitted every pass forever — the intended "already recorded, do nothing" suppression is dead code, so the finding is neither deduplicated across passes nor rate-limited the way the change promises.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/healthwatch.py:87

chunk_findings.detail: The change exposes the watchdog under the config key `health.stall_s` and the CLI command `ddflow health` with `--mode {off,propose,apply}` (help: "override [health].mode"), but the stated intent specifies the section `[watch]` (`[watch].stall_s`, `[watch].idle_s`, `[watch].reply_s`, `[watch].crash_s`, `[watch].interval_s`, `[watch].act`), the mode vocabulary `off | advise | act` with default `advise`, and the CLI surface `ddflow watch inspect|status|history|ack`. Given input where an operator follows the documented configuration (a project file with `[watch] stall_s = 600`, or invokes `ddflow watch inspect`), nothing is read and no command exists — the watchdog threshold and mode are never applied. Either the implemented names/verbs must be reconciled with the documented `[watch]`/`watch`/`advise|act` surface, or the spec-facing knobs and CLI name are wrong and the feature is unreachable as documented.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/templates/upgrade/unreleased/knob_added.health.stall_s.toml / tests/golden/__snapshots__/test_golden_cli_help.ambr (health command)

chunk_findings.detail: The watchdog surface captured by these snapshots only knows `STALLED`, `LOCKED`, `CRASHED` and `RUNAWAY`, and defines `CRASHED` narrowly as "lease expired over work". The intent requires seven conditions per lane, and in particular `CRASHED = the holder's process or session is gone (lease heartbeats carry pid, host and session id so a dead process is seen in minutes, not after the 30-minute TTL)`. There is no `health.crash_s` (nor `health.idle_s` for IDLE-HEARTBEAT, nor `health.reply_s` for UNRESPONSIVE, nor a `STARVED`/governor knob) in the generated config block, and the tool description lists no IDLE-HEARTBEAT, UNRESPONSIVE or STARVED detector. Concrete failure: an agent process is killed while its lease is still within TTL — the heartbeat pid is gone, but with only the lease-expiry rule the lane produces no CRASHED finding until the lease TTL lapses (the intent's regression case "a dead pid is CRASHED within [watch].crash_s" cannot be satisfied). The same gap means a lane that keeps heart-beating with no other activity, or a nudge/yield that goes unanswered, has no configured limit to trigger on.
chunk_findings.title: tests/golden/__snapshots__/test_golden_mcp_tools.ambr — `ddflow_health` description / tests/golden/__snapshots__/test_golden_outputs.ambr — `health.*` config keys

chunk_findings.detail: `apply` is documented as breaking "a stalled lease another agent is waiting for (… the holder's branch and worktree kept)" while explicitly never killing a process. A stalled lane is by definition lease-current, i.e. its holder process is still alive. Breaking the contended lease therefore frees it for an immediate claim by another agent while the original holder is still running; when the stalled holder wakes and resumes it keeps writing the same item/worktree, giving two concurrent writers on one item. The intent's ladder requires the holder be parked before unblocking (`DX-park-and-resume`: "PARK the lane … so its work is kept") precisely to avoid this; the change's `apply` performs the lease break and auto-order edges without any park/stop step, so the "never discards work / never acts on a lane with progress" guarantee is not preserved once the stalled holder resumes.
chunk_findings.title: tests/golden/__snapshots__/test_golden_outputs.ambr — `health.mode` description (the `apply` clause)

chunk_findings.detail: The guard reads only two sources (`Path(HW.__file__)` = `ddflow/services/healthwatch.py` and `Path(H.__file__)` = `ddflow/core/health.py`) and asserts the banned tokens are absent there, with the author's own note that "the module list is deliberately short". But the module where the correction ladder is actually invoked — `ddflow.api.health`, imported at the top of this very file and called as `health(repo, now=later, run=True, mode="apply")` in `test_a_runaway_job_is_reported_and_its_process_is_never_signalled` — is not scanned, nor is the `health --run` CLI command or the hook/scheduler entry points. The property the test claims to establish ("the watchdog has no process kill or delete path", docstring line "never kills a process or deletes work") is therefore not established: add e.g. `os.kill(pid, ...)`/`subprocess.run([...])`/`Path(tree).unlink()` inside `apply_move` in `ddflow/api/health.py` and this test still passes while the watchdog now signals a process or deletes work. (The same substring approach is also over-broad in the other direction: it forbids `os.kill(pid, 0)`, the standard error-checking-only liveness probe, and the bare word `subprocess`, which the stated progress signal "commits in its worktree" may legitimately need — so it can both miss real destruction and fail on harmless code.)
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_health_watch.py::test_the_watchdog_has_no_process_kill_or_delete_path

chunk_findings.detail: The change adds exactly one new config section and bumps the documented total from 270 to 275, i.e. it claims the watchdog section contributes 5 knobs. The watchdog spec attached to this change names six distinct knobs on that section: `stall_s` (STALLED), `idle_s` (IDLE-HEARTBEAT), `reply_s` (UNRESPONSIVE), `interval_s` (throttle), `act` (the mode ladder, one mode per step/finding kind) and `crash_s` (CRASHED within the limit). With the watchdog wired in as the spec describes, the count must be 276 and the section 6 knobs; with the count as written, one of the six documented limits (`crash_s`, `reply_s` or `interval_s`) is missing from the page and from the generated knob table. Concrete failure: `ddflow config --explain <the omitted key>` / `ddflow config --set <key>` has nothing to resolve, and the README test that asserts the printed count cannot agree with a 276-knob config.
chunk_findings.location: README.md:5658 (`275 knobs across 34 sections`, and the `[export] knobs (5 of the 275)` line at README.md:5147)
chunk_findings.title: README.md:5658 (`275 knobs across 34 sections`, and the `[export] knobs (5 of the 275)` line at README.md:5147)

chunk_findings.detail: The documented user-facing surface contradicts the surface in the change's own specification: the README advertises the command as `ddflow health` with `--mode off|propose|apply` and the section as `[health]`, while the change defines the CLI as `ddflow watch inspect|status|history|ack`, the mode ladder as `[watch].act = off|advise|act` with default `advise`, and the knob namespace as `[watch].*`. Following the README, an operator runs `ddflow health --run --mode apply`; following the spec, `ddflow watch status` / `--mode act`. At most one of the two can exist, so one of them is a dead command/mode and an unknown-key error (`propose`/`apply` are not `advise`/`act`, and `[health]` is not `[watch]`). The row also never mentions the `inspect`, `status`, `history` or `ack` subcommands that the change lists as the CLI surface (including `history`/`ack` needed for `DX-doctor-ack`).
chunk_findings.title: README.md:207 (the `ddflow health` summary row)

chunk_findings.detail: The change deletes the `"mode"` property from the `ddflow_health` MCP tool's `inputSchema` (the `-         "mode": { "type": "string", "description": "Override [health].mode for this call: off, propose or apply." }` block), leaving only `run` and `as_agent`. The stated intent makes mode a per-call override that must be reachable from every surface — "CONFORMANCE (D-universal-principles, r-everything-configurable, r-company-workflows): every limit, mode and interval a knob settable by file, CLI, MCP and prompt" — and the mode ladder itself is described as "a mode per step ([watch].act = off | advise | act ...)". After this change an MCP client can only pass `run: true` and is forced onto whatever `[health].mode` happens to be in config; there is no way to invoke an `advise`/`act` pass per call through MCP, which is exactly the knob the intent says must be settable via MCP. The removed property is the only mechanism shown for that, so a harness driving ddflow over MCP cannot perform a one-off apply or downgrade a pass to propose.
chunk_findings.title: tests/golden/__snapshots__/test_golden_mcp_tools.ambr (ddflow_health tool schema)

chunk_findings.detail: The watchdog's config surface, as now frozen into the golden transcript, is only `health.mode`, `health.stall_s`, `health.runaway_s`, `health.interval_s` and `health.shown`. The change's own specification requires a knob for the other inspection conditions and for the correction ladder: IDLE-HEARTBEAT is defined as "renewals continue but nothing else for [watch].idle_s", UNRESPONSIVE as "a nudge or yield request went unanswered for [watch].reply_s", CRASHED as "a dead pid is seen within [watch].crash_s", and the ladder requires "a mode per step ([watch].act = off | advise | act, ... per finding kind)". Concretely, a project that wants `health.mode = 'act'` only for LOCKED/CRASHED but advise for STALLED cannot express that (single global `mode`), and a project that wants an idle-heartbeat lane flagged after 10 minutes rather than reusing `stall_s = 3600` has no `idle_s`/`reply_s`/`crash_s` to set, so those detectors are either absent or hard-coded. Since this transcript is the enumerated output of `ddflow config` (every default-bearing key is listed), the absence is not a rendering artifact. This breaks the change's stated conformance requirement that "every limit, mode and interval [be] a knob settable by file, CLI, MCP and prompt, per project and org" [r-everything-configurable / CONFORMANCE], which is the only part of the guidance that reaches this file.
chunk_findings.location: tests/test_uc_surf_setup_ops_transcript.json:1430 (the `health.*` block in the `ddflow config` golden transcript)
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_uc_surf_setup_ops_transcript.json:1430 (the `health.*` block in the `ddflow config` golden transcript)

chunk_findings.detail: The fixture now claims "117 tools, the same on the CLI and over MCP" and adds exactly one new entry, `ddflow_health`, under "Looking at it" — but the change's own surface contract is `ddflow watch inspect|status|history|ack` on CLI, MCP and the plain prompt, and no `ddflow_watch` / `ddflow watch` appears anywhere in the new string: not in the tool enumeration (which the sentence "Every one of these is a CLI subcommand and an MCP tool; a test fails if the two surfaces diverge" declares exhaustive) and not in the `ddflow help <topic>` list. The arithmetic is internally consistent (the grouped lists still sum to 117 and the old text summed to 116 with 13 "Looking at it" entries, now 14), so the one-name delta is genuinely the only change: the watchdog command family is simply missing. Given input `ddflow watch inspect`, either the command is unregistered (the required watchdog surfaces do not exist, so requirement (4) SURFACES is unmet) or the binary's `ddflow help` output differs from this recorded transcript and the help/CLI-vs-MCP parity test that consumes this file fails. Either way the fixture and the feature it is supposed to document disagree.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_uc_surf_setup_ops_transcript.json:1588 (help-text fixture, "Everything it can do")

chunk_findings.detail: The old code resolved the effective mode first and then validated it (`mode = mode or cfg.health.mode; if mode not in HW.MODES: ...`), so a bad `[health].mode` coming from the config file/prompt surface produced a clean `O.failed("unknown mode ...")`. The new code skips the check whenever the caller supplied no mode (`mode` is `""`/`None`), because `if mode and ...` is False, and only afterwards does it resolve `mode = mode or cfg.health.mode`. Concretely: with `[health].mode = "advise"` (or any typo, e.g. `"Apply"`) and a call that does not pass `--mode`, `HW.modes(cfg, "")` is built from the invalid value, `active = any(m != "off" ...)` is True, `HW.correct(...)` is invoked with the unknown mode, and the surface returns `O.ok(mode="advise", ran=True)` — a silent no-op/garbage action reported as success, where the previous code failed loudly. The per-kind values produced by `HW.modes` are also never validated anywhere in this path.
chunk_findings.location: ddflow/api/healthwatch.py:47 (`inspect`, the new `if mode and mode not in HW.MODES:` guard)
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/healthwatch.py:47 (`inspect`, the new `if mode and mode not in HW.MODES:` guard)

chunk_findings.detail: The governing note for this change states the ladder stays with `mode off|advise|act` ("The ladder stays: nudge -> ask status -> request yield -> park -> take over/relaunch -> escalate, mode off|advise|act."), but the config surface added here documents `health.mode` as `off | propose | apply` (default `"propose"`) and every per-kind knob as `inherit | off | propose | apply`. With `HW.MODES` used as the acceptor in `inspect`, the mode vocabulary required by the note (`advise`/`act`) is not accepted: an operator configuring `health.mode = "advise"`/`--mode act` hits the `unknown mode` path (or, for the config path, the unvalidated path above) rather than a mode with the documented advise-only / act semantics.
chunk_findings.title: README.md:6046-6059 (`health.mode` / `health.mode_*` rows)

chunk_findings.detail: The new short-circuit decides "the watchdog is off" from `HW.modes(cfg)` alone, but that mapping is exactly the six per-kind modes this same change documents (`mode_idle, mode_stalled, mode_unresponsive, mode_locked, mode_crashed, mode_runaway`) — and the finding set this watchdog is specified to produce has a seventh kind, STARVED (governor/quota pressure), which has no mode of its own and therefore still falls under the base `[health].mode`. Concretely: with `[health] mode = "propose"` (the default) and the six per-kind knobs set to `"off"` — the natural way an operator silences the kinds they know about — `values()` is all `"off"`, `all(...)` is True, and `health_lines` returns `[]` even though the pass still computes STARVED findings under the base mode, so those findings are silently dropped from every surface that calls this helper (brief, status, statusline, doctor). The same vacuity bites the degenerate case: `all()` over an empty mapping is True, so any `cfg` whose health section resolves to no kind modes makes `health_lines` report "nothing stuck" forever, regardless of the base mode. The guard needs to reflect the pass's actual enablement rule (base mode plus per-kind overrides over *all* finding kinds), e.g. only short-circuit when the kind set is known and every effective mode, base included, is `"off"`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/reporting/waitcycles.py:53

chunk_findings.detail: The change's own intent enumerates seven finding kinds — STALLED, IDLE‑HEARTBEAT, LOCKED, CRASHED, RUNAWAY, UNRESPONSIVE and STARVED — and says the correction is "a ladder with a mode per step (… per finding kind)" and that, per its conformance line, "every limit, mode and interval [is] a knob settable by file, CLI, MCP and prompt, per project and org". This diff adds per‑kind mode knobs for only six kinds: `mode_idle`, `mode_stalled`, `mode_unresponsive`, `mode_locked`, `mode_crashed`, `mode_runaway`. There is no `mode_starved` (and nothing else in the section keys a mode by the `starved` kind). Given a lane the governor samples as under context/quota pressure, the watchdog has no per‑kind mode to resolve: the operator cannot turn starved findings off, cannot promote them to `apply`, and cannot give them a mode independent of the global `[health].mode` the way they can for every other inspected condition. Either the correction resolver must special‑case `starved` (making its behaviour unconfigurable, contrary to the per‑kind mode contract), or it will resolve a mode for a kind that has no knob. Every other kind the intent lists is covered, so the omission is not a deliberate exclusion pattern.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/config_sections/health.py (the added `mode_*` knobs)

chunk_findings.detail: `_dead` is the builder for the newly added CRASHED case of "a **live** lease whose holder's process is gone" (module docstring), i.e. a lease that is still *current* (the process died before the 30-minute TTL elapsed), yet the corrective command it prints is a plain `ddflow claim {ln.item}`. A plain claim cannot take a lease that is still live: the sibling `_unresponsive`, which describes exactly the same "live lease, holder not cooperating" state, has to pass `--break` (`ddflow claim {waiters[0]} --break`) to take it. Input: a lane whose pid has exited and whose lease was last renewed `crash_s` ago but has not expired → the finding is raised, the operator pastes the printed `ddflow claim <item>`, and it is refused, so the lane stays held until the 30-minute TTL runs out — precisely the outcome the intent was written to avoid ("a dead process is seen in minutes, not after the 30-minute TTL"). The command needs the park/break step (DX-park-and-resume / DX-dispatch-supervise) before the claim, as `_unresponsive` does.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/core/health.py: `_dead`

chunk_findings.detail: `Lane.asked_at` is documented as "when the newest nudge or stop request for this lease was made; 0.0 for none" and defaults to `0.0`, but `_unresponsive` does `asked = now - lane.asked_at` with no sentinel test (the same holds for `renewed_at` in `_dead`). Input: any `Lane` that has never been asked — the documented "none" state, and the field's default — reaches the helper and yields `asked ≈ 1.7e9` s: the finding's detail becomes "asked 56 years ago, no progress and no release since" and its evidence carries `asked_s ≈ 1.75e9`, and when `waiters` is non-empty the ladder will park the lane and break a claim. `_idle` avoids this because it receives the already-computed `age`; `_unresponsive`/`_dead` must likewise test the sentinel (`asked_at > 0`, `renewed_at > 0`) instead of treating "0.0 for none" as an epoch timestamp, or the "none" value must not be a usable number.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/core/health.py: `_unresponsive` (and `_dead`)

chunk_findings.location: `ddflow/services/healthwatch.py` / `_stalled_move` (the `if now - asked >= cfg.health.reply_s:  return None` branch)
chunk_findings.title: `ddflow/services/healthwatch.py` / `_stalled_move` (the `if now - asked >= cfg.health.reply_s:  return None` branch)

chunk_findings.detail: The intent defines the watchdog's inspected conditions as seven finding kinds — STALLED, IDLE-HEARTBEAT, LOCKED, CRASHED, RUNAWAY, UNRESPONSIVE and STARVED — and requires a corrective ladder "with a mode per step (…, per finding kind)" that is "settable by file, CLI, MCP and prompt" (r-everything-configurable). This change adds per-kind mode knobs for six of the seven kinds (`health.mode_crashed`, `health.mode_idle`, `health.mode_locked`, `health.mode_runaway`, `health.mode_stalled`, `health.mode_unresponsive`) but none for the starved kind. The templates in this hunk are sorted by full path (`mode_runaway` → `mode_stalled` → `mode_unresponsive`), and `health.mode_starved.toml` would sort exactly between `health.mode_stalled.toml` and `health.mode_unresponsive.toml`; since both neighbours are present in this same contiguous hunk, the absence is a real gap, not an artifact of the diff being split into parts (unlike `health.mode`, `health.stall_s`, `health.crash_s`, `health.interval_s`, which sort before `health.idle_s` and could legitimately sit in an earlier part). Consequence for a user: a `STARVED` finding (context/quota pressure from the governor, P-governor.sampling) has no `health.mode_starved` value to read, so its behaviour cannot be set to `off | advise | act` independently as the other kinds can — e.g. an operator who sets `health.mode_starved = "off"` in the project or org file has the setting silently ignored/unknown, while the same setting for `health.mode_stalled` works.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/templates/upgrade/unreleased/ (health.mode_starved missing)

chunk_findings.detail: The `ddflow_health` tool's `inputSchema.properties` loses `"mode"` (previously `"Override [health].mode for this call: off, propose or apply."`) while `"additionalProperties": false` is kept and the rewritten description still advertises mode control — `"run": { "description": "Correct per mode." }` and the tool description `"run=true corrects per [health].mode and the mode_<kind> overrides"`. Since the schema is the contract an MCP client validates against, an existing caller that sends `{"name":"ddflow_health","arguments":{"run":true,"mode":"apply"}}` (which the previous snapshot explicitly documented and accepted) is now rejected by schema validation, and no per-call replacement is offered: `mode_<kind>` is named only as a config key, not as any parameter on this tool, and the tool's own description no longer states that a per-call override exists. The change's stated conformance requires that "every limit, mode and interval a knob settable by file, CLI, MCP and prompt" ([r-everything-configurable]), so dropping the only mode input on the watchdog MCP tool removes the MCP leg of that requirement and silently changes the behavior of any caller that previously passed `mode`. If the intent was to move mode control to config-only, the tool description ("Correct per mode", "mode_<kind> overrides") is left asserting a capability the schema no longer expresses, which is the inconsistency an MCP client will trip over.
chunk_findings.title: tests/golden/__snapshots__/test_golden_mcp_tools.ambr (ddflow_health inputSchema, ~line 1233)

chunk_findings.detail: The new help text defines the per-kind mode knobs as taking `'off'`, `'propose'` or `'apply'` (and states an unrecognised value falls back to `'propose'`). The governing roadmap review note for this change states the ladder "mode off|advise|act", so the documented vocabulary here is wrong and, worse, actively defeats the feature. Concrete input: an operator who follows the design configures `health.mode_stalled = 'act'` (or `'advise'`); the code path described treats `'act'` as a typo, emits a warning, has `doctor` report it, and silently downgrades to `'propose'`, so a stalled lane is only reported and never parked/taken over. The key name and values therefore contradict the authoritative interface (`off | advise | act`, default `advise`), meaning every setting written per the roadmap is rejected and the watchdog never reaches its acting rungs. Either the snapshot (and the parsing/validation code it reflects) uses the wrong value set, or the note is stale; as written, the two cannot both be true, and the note is stated to govern.
chunk_findings.title: tests/golden/__snapshots__/test_golden_outputs.ambr (health.mode_* entries, added block at ~line 1663+)

chunk_findings.detail: The test was renamed to claim the watchdog "parks then breaks", and the new comment says `# parked before it was broken`, but no assertion actually establishes that ordering. The park check collects only park subjects (`_records(repo, "health_park:") == ["health_park:T1"]`) and the break check independently counts break events (`len(broke) == 1 and broke[0].data["broken_by"] == "ddflow:health"`); neither compares positions in the event log. Concretely, if the implementation expired/broke the lease first and parked agent-a afterwards, both lists still have exactly one matching entry, `st.items["T1"].lease.expired_at` is still set, and `(tree / "unfinished.py")` still reads "# nowhere else\n", so every assertion passes even though the safety property the rename asserts — parking the lane so its work is kept *before* the lease is broken — is violated. A regression that reverses park and break would therefore go undetected; the test should assert the park event's index precedes the break event's index in `EventLog(repo, "r").read_all()`.

chunk_findings.detail: The change deletes the only regression test that enforced the watchdog's destructive-action ban. The removed test read the source of the health/watchdog modules and asserted that none of `os.kill`, `killpg`, `rmtree`, `W.remove`, `unlink(` or `subprocess` appear anywhere in them, with the explicit comment that "the check above is the point". Nothing in the replacement tests reinstates that property: the new cases (`test_a_dead_harness_is_crashed_in_a_real_repo_and_apply_records_the_expiry`, `test_unresponsive_after_reply_s_parks_then_breaks_and_keeps_the_work`) assert only that a single sentinel file in one worktree survives one particular ladder step, and they now *import and call* `subprocess` in the test module itself rather than policing the product modules. Concretely: if the park/take-over/escalate path is later (or already) implemented with `shutil.rmtree(lease.worktree)` or `os.kill(pid, SIGKILL)` — exactly the destructive primitives the removed test forbade — every test in this file still passes, even though the intent states the ladder must "Never discards work, never acts on a lane with progress" and every step must be "reversible". The removal of this invariant is not compensated by any assertion in the diff, so the safety guarantee the watchdog is built around is now untested.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_health_watch.py (removed `test_the_watchdog_has_no_process_kill_or_delete_path`)

chunk_findings.detail: The scan's only exemption is `name == "kill"`, but signal 0 ("null signal") is the POSIX existence probe for every process-signalling API in `KILLERS`, not just `os.kill`. `os.killpg(pgid, 0)` (line 38 lists `killpg`) and `Popen.send_signal(0)` (listed as `send_signal`) end nothing — they only test whether the group/child exists — yet `_is_probe` returns False for them, so `test_every_process_signal_in_ddflow_is_on_a_child_it_started` reports them as "unreviewed process-signalling call(s)". Concrete failure: a liveness helper like `def alive(pgid): return os.killpg(pgid, 0) == 0` anywhere in `ddflow/` outside the six listed functions fails the suite even though the call cannot end a process, contradicting the test's own docstring ("every call that can end a process ... must be one of the sites below").
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_no_kill_paths.py:62-69 (`_is_probe`)

chunk_findings.detail: The `replace`/`move` carve-out only recognizes a *literal* receiver (`ast.Constant`/`ast.JoinedStr`), so `.replace(...)` on a string held in a variable, an attribute, or a concatenation is treated as a deletion in `test_the_watchdog_modules_signal_nothing_and_delete_nothing`. Concrete failure: `core/health.py` line `evidence = tpl.replace("{lane}", lane)` (or `msg = self.summary.replace(", ", ";")`) is appended to `bad` as `replace() in ...` although no file is touched, and `assert not bad` fails; the same over-match applies to `remove`/`move` on in-memory containers, e.g. `findings.remove(f)`, which get no exemption at all even though they delete no work. The exemption is thus incomplete for the very case it was written to cover.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_no_kill_paths.py:97 and 102-105 (`_is_str_call`)

chunk_findings.detail: The golden config registered here records the watchdog's global correction mode as `health.mode = 'propose'`. The watchdog interface it is supposed to render fixes this knob as `[watch].act = off | advise | act, default advise` (intent section 3; conformance r-everything-configurable). A project that follows the documented interface and sets the mode to the documented middle value `advise` is addressing a value that does not appear in the recorded knob space, and the shipped default `propose` is not one of the three documented ladder modes. The transcript is the golden rendering of the registered config, so either the default/value set must be `off | advise | act` with `advise`, or the spec's documented value set is wrong; as recorded, the two disagree.

chunk_findings.detail: The change adds per-finding-kind mode overrides for exactly six of the watchdog's conditions — `health.mode_idle`, `health.mode_stalled`, `health.mode_unresponsive`, `health.mode_locked`, `health.mode_crashed`, `health.mode_runaway` — but no override for STARVED, even though STARVED is listed in section 1 as one of the conditions every lane must be inspected for ("STARVED = context or quota pressure from the governor"). Likewise there is no other `health.*` key covering starved lanes. Because the requirement is that "every limit, mode and interval [is] a knob settable by file, CLI, MCP and prompt, per project and org" and that the correction ladder's mode is set "per finding kind", a starved lane's step cannot be configured to off/advise/act at all. A `health.mode_starved = 'inherit'` entry is missing from the recorded default config.

chunk_findings.detail: `health_lines` is the single funnel this change wires into the surfaces: `overview.py` uses it for `data["health"]`, and `wait_order` appends it to the doctor `notes`. Its filter unconditionally discards every finding whose `kind` is `H.CRASHED` (and every finding whose `evidence["via"] == "cycle"`), so the fastest crash signal the watchdog produces never reaches any of these surfaces. Concrete input: a lane holding a live, being-renewed lease whose heartbeat reports a pid/host/session that no longer exist (or is being renewed by a straggling heartbeat loop, the 2026-10-15 "stopped agent" case). `HW.inspect` returns a finding of kind `H.CRASHED`; `health_lines` drops it because `f.kind != H.CRASHED` is False, so `data["health"]` in the status/overview payload and the doctor notes are empty for that lane, and the brief/statusline/dispatcher-plan consumers built on them see nothing — even though the stated intent makes CRASHED ("the holder's process or session is gone ... so a dead process is seen in minutes, not after the 30-minute TTL") a required inspected condition with a correction step ("take over or relaunch from the worktree"). The docstring's justification, "Finding lines not already shown elsewhere", does not hold for this case: the only other lease-related surface (`recoverable`) covers the lease-expired-with-work case, not a dead pid behind a still-valid lease, so a crashed lane stays invisible until the TTL lapses, which is exactly the detection latency this change is supposed to remove.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/reporting/waitcycles.py:health_lines (the `f.kind != H.CRASHED` filter, ~line 57)

chunk_findings.detail: The section only exposes limits for two of the conditions the watchdog must detect: `stall_s` (STALLED) and `runaway_s` (RUNAWAY). The change's own specification names three further required knobs — `[watch].idle_s` for IDLE-HEARTBEAT ("renewals continue but nothing else for [watch].idle_s"), `[watch].reply_s` for UNRESPONSIVE ("a nudge or yield request went unanswered for [watch].reply_s") and `[watch].crash_s` for CRASHED ("a dead pid is CRASHED within [watch].crash_s ... seen in minutes, not after the 30-minute TTL") — and its CONFORMANCE clause requires "every limit, mode and interval a knob settable by file, CLI, MCP and prompt, per project and org" [r-everything-configurable]. With this section as written, an operator can set how long a *lease-renewing* lane may make no progress (`stall_s`) but cannot set the dead-pid/session-gone detection window, the idle-heartbeat window, or the nudge-reply window: those can only be hard-coded, so the very "seen in minutes" behaviour the operator asked for is not configurable (e.g. setting `[health].crash_s = 120` has no field to bind to and is silently ignored / rejected, and the watchdog cannot be tuned faster than its built-in threshold). The class docstring even claims it covers "stalled, locked, crashed and runaway lanes" while crash has no knob at all.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/config_sections/health.py:12-42 (HealthConfig knobs)

chunk_findings.detail: `mode` is a single string applied to every finding kind, but the specification requires the correction mode to be settable *per finding kind* ("a mode per step ([watch].act = off | advise | act, default advise, per finding kind)"): an operator must be able to, say, leave lock/cycle findings at `propose` while letting a CRASHED lane's lease be expired in `apply`, or run `apply` for runaways only. With one global field, `[health].mode = "apply"` turns on lease-breaking and `needs`-edge insertion for *all* kinds at once, so there is no configuration under which the documented ladder is applied selectively as specified; a project that wants detection-and-report for deadlocks but automatic recovery for crashes cannot express it.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/config_sections/health.py:15-21 (HealthConfig.mode)

chunk_findings.detail: `recorded` is computed as `not lz.live(lz.renewed_at)`. A lease is always live at its own renewal instant (`renewed_at < renewed_at + ttl [+ grace]`), so this expression is `False` for every lane, live or expired, regardless of what the log holds. The comment says "an expiry is recorded, whatever the clock says", but the value never consults the log at all — even though the record that actually answers the question is already sitting right there in `rec` (`recs.get(i)`, line 85, keyed on `kind == "expired_lease"`). Concretely: take a lane whose process died leaving work, whose lease has expired and for which `L.scan` already yields an `expired_lease` record (so `rec is not None`, `work is True`). `gather` still hands `H.Lane(..., work=True, recorded=False, ...)`, so `correct`'s guard `f.evidence.get("work") is True and not f.evidence["recorded"]` (line ~163) is always satisfied. In `apply` mode `L.expire` is therefore re-invoked for an already-expired lane on every watchdog pass, and in `propose` mode a "would record ... expired" line is emitted every pass forever — the intended "already recorded, do nothing" suppression is dead code, so the finding is neither deduplicated across passes nor rate-limited the way the change promises.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/healthwatch.py:87

chunk_findings.detail: The change exposes the watchdog under the config key `health.stall_s` and the CLI command `ddflow health` with `--mode {off,propose,apply}` (help: "override [health].mode"), but the stated intent specifies the section `[watch]` (`[watch].stall_s`, `[watch].idle_s`, `[watch].reply_s`, `[watch].crash_s`, `[watch].interval_s`, `[watch].act`), the mode vocabulary `off | advise | act` with default `advise`, and the CLI surface `ddflow watch inspect|status|history|ack`. Given input where an operator follows the documented configuration (a project file with `[watch] stall_s = 600`, or invokes `ddflow watch inspect`), nothing is read and no command exists — the watchdog threshold and mode are never applied. Either the implemented names/verbs must be reconciled with the documented `[watch]`/`watch`/`advise|act` surface, or the spec-facing knobs and CLI name are wrong and the feature is unreachable as documented.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/templates/upgrade/unreleased/knob_added.health.stall_s.toml / tests/golden/__snapshots__/test_golden_cli_help.ambr (health command)

chunk_findings.detail: The watchdog surface captured by these snapshots only knows `STALLED`, `LOCKED`, `CRASHED` and `RUNAWAY`, and defines `CRASHED` narrowly as "lease expired over work". The intent requires seven conditions per lane, and in particular `CRASHED = the holder's process or session is gone (lease heartbeats carry pid, host and session id so a dead process is seen in minutes, not after the 30-minute TTL)`. There is no `health.crash_s` (nor `health.idle_s` for IDLE-HEARTBEAT, nor `health.reply_s` for UNRESPONSIVE, nor a `STARVED`/governor knob) in the generated config block, and the tool description lists no IDLE-HEARTBEAT, UNRESPONSIVE or STARVED detector. Concrete failure: an agent process is killed while its lease is still within TTL — the heartbeat pid is gone, but with only the lease-expiry rule the lane produces no CRASHED finding until the lease TTL lapses (the intent's regression case "a dead pid is CRASHED within [watch].crash_s" cannot be satisfied). The same gap means a lane that keeps heart-beating with no other activity, or a nudge/yield that goes unanswered, has no configured limit to trigger on.
chunk_findings.title: tests/golden/__snapshots__/test_golden_mcp_tools.ambr — `ddflow_health` description / tests/golden/__snapshots__/test_golden_outputs.ambr — `health.*` config keys

chunk_findings.detail: `apply` is documented as breaking "a stalled lease another agent is waiting for (… the holder's branch and worktree kept)" while explicitly never killing a process. A stalled lane is by definition lease-current, i.e. its holder process is still alive. Breaking the contended lease therefore frees it for an immediate claim by another agent while the original holder is still running; when the stalled holder wakes and resumes it keeps writing the same item/worktree, giving two concurrent writers on one item. The intent's ladder requires the holder be parked before unblocking (`DX-park-and-resume`: "PARK the lane … so its work is kept") precisely to avoid this; the change's `apply` performs the lease break and auto-order edges without any park/stop step, so the "never discards work / never acts on a lane with progress" guarantee is not preserved once the stalled holder resumes.
chunk_findings.title: tests/golden/__snapshots__/test_golden_outputs.ambr — `health.mode` description (the `apply` clause)

chunk_findings.detail: The guard reads only two sources (`Path(HW.__file__)` = `ddflow/services/healthwatch.py` and `Path(H.__file__)` = `ddflow/core/health.py`) and asserts the banned tokens are absent there, with the author's own note that "the module list is deliberately short". But the module where the correction ladder is actually invoked — `ddflow.api.health`, imported at the top of this very file and called as `health(repo, now=later, run=True, mode="apply")` in `test_a_runaway_job_is_reported_and_its_process_is_never_signalled` — is not scanned, nor is the `health --run` CLI command or the hook/scheduler entry points. The property the test claims to establish ("the watchdog has no process kill or delete path", docstring line "never kills a process or deletes work") is therefore not established: add e.g. `os.kill(pid, ...)`/`subprocess.run([...])`/`Path(tree).unlink()` inside `apply_move` in `ddflow/api/health.py` and this test still passes while the watchdog now signals a process or deletes work. (The same substring approach is also over-broad in the other direction: it forbids `os.kill(pid, 0)`, the standard error-checking-only liveness probe, and the bare word `subprocess`, which the stated progress signal "commits in its worktree" may legitimately need — so it can both miss real destruction and fail on harmless code.)
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_health_watch.py::test_the_watchdog_has_no_process_kill_or_delete_path

chunk_findings.detail: The change adds exactly one new config section and bumps the documented total from 270 to 275, i.e. it claims the watchdog section contributes 5 knobs. The watchdog spec attached to this change names six distinct knobs on that section: `stall_s` (STALLED), `idle_s` (IDLE-HEARTBEAT), `reply_s` (UNRESPONSIVE), `interval_s` (throttle), `act` (the mode ladder, one mode per step/finding kind) and `crash_s` (CRASHED within the limit). With the watchdog wired in as the spec describes, the count must be 276 and the section 6 knobs; with the count as written, one of the six documented limits (`crash_s`, `reply_s` or `interval_s`) is missing from the page and from the generated knob table. Concrete failure: `ddflow config --explain <the omitted key>` / `ddflow config --set <key>` has nothing to resolve, and the README test that asserts the printed count cannot agree with a 276-knob config.

chunk_findings.detail: The documented user-facing surface contradicts the surface in the change's own specification: the README advertises the command as `ddflow health` with `--mode off|propose|apply` and the section as `[health]`, while the change defines the CLI as `ddflow watch inspect|status|history|ack`, the mode ladder as `[watch].act = off|advise|act` with default `advise`, and the knob namespace as `[watch].*`. Following the README, an operator runs `ddflow health --run --mode apply`; following the spec, `ddflow watch status` / `--mode act`. At most one of the two can exist, so one of them is a dead command/mode and an unknown-key error (`propose`/`apply` are not `advise`/`act`, and `[health]` is not `[watch]`). The row also never mentions the `inspect`, `status`, `history` or `ack` subcommands that the change lists as the CLI surface (including `history`/`ack` needed for `DX-doctor-ack`).
chunk_findings.title: README.md:207 (the `ddflow health` summary row)

chunk_findings.detail: The change deletes the `"mode"` property from the `ddflow_health` MCP tool's `inputSchema` (the `-         "mode": { "type": "string", "description": "Override [health].mode for this call: off, propose or apply." }` block), leaving only `run` and `as_agent`. The stated intent makes mode a per-call override that must be reachable from every surface — "CONFORMANCE (D-universal-principles, r-everything-configurable, r-company-workflows): every limit, mode and interval a knob settable by file, CLI, MCP and prompt" — and the mode ladder itself is described as "a mode per step ([watch].act = off | advise | act ...)". After this change an MCP client can only pass `run: true` and is forced onto whatever `[health].mode` happens to be in config; there is no way to invoke an `advise`/`act` pass per call through MCP, which is exactly the knob the intent says must be settable via MCP. The removed property is the only mechanism shown for that, so a harness driving ddflow over MCP cannot perform a one-off apply or downgrade a pass to propose.
chunk_findings.title: tests/golden/__snapshots__/test_golden_mcp_tools.ambr (ddflow_health tool schema)

chunk_findings.detail: The watchdog's config surface, as now frozen into the golden transcript, is only `health.mode`, `health.stall_s`, `health.runaway_s`, `health.interval_s` and `health.shown`. The change's own specification requires a knob for the other inspection conditions and for the correction ladder: IDLE-HEARTBEAT is defined as "renewals continue but nothing else for [watch].idle_s", UNRESPONSIVE as "a nudge or yield request went unanswered for [watch].reply_s", CRASHED as "a dead pid is seen within [watch].crash_s", and the ladder requires "a mode per step ([watch].act = off | advise | act, ... per finding kind)". Concretely, a project that wants `health.mode = 'act'` only for LOCKED/CRASHED but advise for STALLED cannot express that (single global `mode`), and a project that wants an idle-heartbeat lane flagged after 10 minutes rather than reusing `stall_s = 3600` has no `idle_s`/`reply_s`/`crash_s` to set, so those detectors are either absent or hard-coded. Since this transcript is the enumerated output of `ddflow config` (every default-bearing key is listed), the absence is not a rendering artifact. This breaks the change's stated conformance requirement that "every limit, mode and interval [be] a knob settable by file, CLI, MCP and prompt, per project and org" [r-everything-configurable / CONFORMANCE], which is the only part of the guidance that reaches this file.
chunk_findings.location: tests/test_uc_surf_setup_ops_transcript.json:1430 (the `health.*` block in the `ddflow config` golden transcript)
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_uc_surf_setup_ops_transcript.json:1430 (the `health.*` block in the `ddflow config` golden transcript)

chunk_findings.detail: The fixture now claims "117 tools, the same on the CLI and over MCP" and adds exactly one new entry, `ddflow_health`, under "Looking at it" — but the change's own surface contract is `ddflow watch inspect|status|history|ack` on CLI, MCP and the plain prompt, and no `ddflow_watch` / `ddflow watch` appears anywhere in the new string: not in the tool enumeration (which the sentence "Every one of these is a CLI subcommand and an MCP tool; a test fails if the two surfaces diverge" declares exhaustive) and not in the `ddflow help <topic>` list. The arithmetic is internally consistent (the grouped lists still sum to 117 and the old text summed to 116 with 13 "Looking at it" entries, now 14), so the one-name delta is genuinely the only change: the watchdog command family is simply missing. Given input `ddflow watch inspect`, either the command is unregistered (the required watchdog surfaces do not exist, so requirement (4) SURFACES is unmet) or the binary's `ddflow help` output differs from this recorded transcript and the help/CLI-vs-MCP parity test that consumes this file fails. Either way the fixture and the feature it is supposed to document disagree.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_uc_surf_setup_ops_transcript.json:1588 (help-text fixture, "Everything it can do")

chunk_findings.detail: The old code resolved the effective mode first and then validated it (`mode = mode or cfg.health.mode; if mode not in HW.MODES: ...`), so a bad `[health].mode` coming from the config file/prompt surface produced a clean `O.failed("unknown mode ...")`. The new code skips the check whenever the caller supplied no mode (`mode` is `""`/`None`), because `if mode and ...` is False, and only afterwards does it resolve `mode = mode or cfg.health.mode`. Concretely: with `[health].mode = "advise"` (or any typo, e.g. `"Apply"`) and a call that does not pass `--mode`, `HW.modes(cfg, "")` is built from the invalid value, `active = any(m != "off" ...)` is True, `HW.correct(...)` is invoked with the unknown mode, and the surface returns `O.ok(mode="advise", ran=True)` — a silent no-op/garbage action reported as success, where the previous code failed loudly. The per-kind values produced by `HW.modes` are also never validated anywhere in this path.
chunk_findings.location: ddflow/api/healthwatch.py:47 (`inspect`, the new `if mode and mode not in HW.MODES:` guard)
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/healthwatch.py:47 (`inspect`, the new `if mode and mode not in HW.MODES:` guard)

chunk_findings.detail: The governing note for this change states the ladder stays with `mode off|advise|act` ("The ladder stays: nudge -> ask status -> request yield -> park -> take over/relaunch -> escalate, mode off|advise|act."), but the config surface added here documents `health.mode` as `off | propose | apply` (default `"propose"`) and every per-kind knob as `inherit | off | propose | apply`. With `HW.MODES` used as the acceptor in `inspect`, the mode vocabulary required by the note (`advise`/`act`) is not accepted: an operator configuring `health.mode = "advise"`/`--mode act` hits the `unknown mode` path (or, for the config path, the unvalidated path above) rather than a mode with the documented advise-only / act semantics.
chunk_findings.title: README.md:6046-6059 (`health.mode` / `health.mode_*` rows)

chunk_findings.detail: The new short-circuit decides "the watchdog is off" from `HW.modes(cfg)` alone, but that mapping is exactly the six per-kind modes this same change documents (`mode_idle, mode_stalled, mode_unresponsive, mode_locked, mode_crashed, mode_runaway`) — and the finding set this watchdog is specified to produce has a seventh kind, STARVED (governor/quota pressure), which has no mode of its own and therefore still falls under the base `[health].mode`. Concretely: with `[health] mode = "propose"` (the default) and the six per-kind knobs set to `"off"` — the natural way an operator silences the kinds they know about — `values()` is all `"off"`, `all(...)` is True, and `health_lines` returns `[]` even though the pass still computes STARVED findings under the base mode, so those findings are silently dropped from every surface that calls this helper (brief, status, statusline, doctor). The same vacuity bites the degenerate case: `all()` over an empty mapping is True, so any `cfg` whose health section resolves to no kind modes makes `health_lines` report "nothing stuck" forever, regardless of the base mode. The guard needs to reflect the pass's actual enablement rule (base mode plus per-kind overrides over *all* finding kinds), e.g. only short-circuit when the kind set is known and every effective mode, base included, is `"off"`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/reporting/waitcycles.py:53

chunk_findings.detail: The change's own intent enumerates seven finding kinds — STALLED, IDLE‑HEARTBEAT, LOCKED, CRASHED, RUNAWAY, UNRESPONSIVE and STARVED — and says the correction is "a ladder with a mode per step (… per finding kind)" and that, per its conformance line, "every limit, mode and interval [is] a knob settable by file, CLI, MCP and prompt, per project and org". This diff adds per‑kind mode knobs for only six kinds: `mode_idle`, `mode_stalled`, `mode_unresponsive`, `mode_locked`, `mode_crashed`, `mode_runaway`. There is no `mode_starved` (and nothing else in the section keys a mode by the `starved` kind). Given a lane the governor samples as under context/quota pressure, the watchdog has no per‑kind mode to resolve: the operator cannot turn starved findings off, cannot promote them to `apply`, and cannot give them a mode independent of the global `[health].mode` the way they can for every other inspected condition. Either the correction resolver must special‑case `starved` (making its behaviour unconfigurable, contrary to the per‑kind mode contract), or it will resolve a mode for a kind that has no knob. Every other kind the intent lists is covered, so the omission is not a deliberate exclusion pattern.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/config_sections/health.py (the added `mode_*` knobs)

chunk_findings.detail: `_dead` is the builder for the newly added CRASHED case of "a **live** lease whose holder's process is gone" (module docstring), i.e. a lease that is still *current* (the process died before the 30-minute TTL elapsed), yet the corrective command it prints is a plain `ddflow claim {ln.item}`. A plain claim cannot take a lease that is still live: the sibling `_unresponsive`, which describes exactly the same "live lease, holder not cooperating" state, has to pass `--break` (`ddflow claim {waiters[0]} --break`) to take it. Input: a lane whose pid has exited and whose lease was last renewed `crash_s` ago but has not expired → the finding is raised, the operator pastes the printed `ddflow claim <item>`, and it is refused, so the lane stays held until the 30-minute TTL runs out — precisely the outcome the intent was written to avoid ("a dead process is seen in minutes, not after the 30-minute TTL"). The command needs the park/break step (DX-park-and-resume / DX-dispatch-supervise) before the claim, as `_unresponsive` does.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/core/health.py: `_dead`

chunk_findings.detail: `Lane.asked_at` is documented as "when the newest nudge or stop request for this lease was made; 0.0 for none" and defaults to `0.0`, but `_unresponsive` does `asked = now - lane.asked_at` with no sentinel test (the same holds for `renewed_at` in `_dead`). Input: any `Lane` that has never been asked — the documented "none" state, and the field's default — reaches the helper and yields `asked ≈ 1.7e9` s: the finding's detail becomes "asked 56 years ago, no progress and no release since" and its evidence carries `asked_s ≈ 1.75e9`, and when `waiters` is non-empty the ladder will park the lane and break a claim. `_idle` avoids this because it receives the already-computed `age`; `_unresponsive`/`_dead` must likewise test the sentinel (`asked_at > 0`, `renewed_at > 0`) instead of treating "0.0 for none" as an epoch timestamp, or the "none" value must not be a usable number.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/core/health.py: `_unresponsive` (and `_dead`)

chunk_findings.detail: The intent defines the watchdog's inspected conditions as seven finding kinds — STALLED, IDLE-HEARTBEAT, LOCKED, CRASHED, RUNAWAY, UNRESPONSIVE and STARVED — and requires a corrective ladder "with a mode per step (…, per finding kind)" that is "settable by file, CLI, MCP and prompt" (r-everything-configurable). This change adds per-kind mode knobs for six of the seven kinds (`health.mode_crashed`, `health.mode_idle`, `health.mode_locked`, `health.mode_runaway`, `health.mode_stalled`, `health.mode_unresponsive`) but none for the starved kind. The templates in this hunk are sorted by full path (`mode_runaway` → `mode_stalled` → `mode_unresponsive`), and `health.mode_starved.toml` would sort exactly between `health.mode_stalled.toml` and `health.mode_unresponsive.toml`; since both neighbours are present in this same contiguous hunk, the absence is a real gap, not an artifact of the diff being split into parts (unlike `health.mode`, `health.stall_s`, `health.crash_s`, `health.interval_s`, which sort before `health.idle_s` and could legitimately sit in an earlier part). Consequence for a user: a `STARVED` finding (context/quota pressure from the governor, P-governor.sampling) has no `health.mode_starved` value to read, so its behaviour cannot be set to `off | advise | act` independently as the other kinds can — e.g. an operator who sets `health.mode_starved = "off"` in the project or org file has the setting silently ignored/unknown, while the same setting for `health.mode_stalled` works.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/templates/upgrade/unreleased/ (health.mode_starved missing)

chunk_findings.detail: The `ddflow_health` tool's `inputSchema.properties` loses `"mode"` (previously `"Override [health].mode for this call: off, propose or apply."`) while `"additionalProperties": false` is kept and the rewritten description still advertises mode control — `"run": { "description": "Correct per mode." }` and the tool description `"run=true corrects per [health].mode and the mode_<kind> overrides"`. Since the schema is the contract an MCP client validates against, an existing caller that sends `{"name":"ddflow_health","arguments":{"run":true,"mode":"apply"}}` (which the previous snapshot explicitly documented and accepted) is now rejected by schema validation, and no per-call replacement is offered: `mode_<kind>` is named only as a config key, not as any parameter on this tool, and the tool's own description no longer states that a per-call override exists. The change's stated conformance requires that "every limit, mode and interval a knob settable by file, CLI, MCP and prompt" ([r-everything-configurable]), so dropping the only mode input on the watchdog MCP tool removes the MCP leg of that requirement and silently changes the behavior of any caller that previously passed `mode`. If the intent was to move mode control to config-only, the tool description ("Correct per mode", "mode_<kind> overrides") is left asserting a capability the schema no longer expresses, which is the inconsistency an MCP client will trip over.
chunk_findings.title: tests/golden/__snapshots__/test_golden_mcp_tools.ambr (ddflow_health inputSchema, ~line 1233)

chunk_findings.detail: The new help text defines the per-kind mode knobs as taking `'off'`, `'propose'` or `'apply'` (and states an unrecognised value falls back to `'propose'`). The governing roadmap review note for this change states the ladder "mode off|advise|act", so the documented vocabulary here is wrong and, worse, actively defeats the feature. Concrete input: an operator who follows the design configures `health.mode_stalled = 'act'` (or `'advise'`); the code path described treats `'act'` as a typo, emits a warning, has `doctor` report it, and silently downgrades to `'propose'`, so a stalled lane is only reported and never parked/taken over. The key name and values therefore contradict the authoritative interface (`off | advise | act`, default `advise`), meaning every setting written per the roadmap is rejected and the watchdog never reaches its acting rungs. Either the snapshot (and the parsing/validation code it reflects) uses the wrong value set, or the note is stale; as written, the two cannot both be true, and the note is stated to govern.
chunk_findings.title: tests/golden/__snapshots__/test_golden_outputs.ambr (health.mode_* entries, added block at ~line 1663+)

chunk_findings.detail: The test was renamed to claim the watchdog "parks then breaks", and the new comment says `# parked before it was broken`, but no assertion actually establishes that ordering. The park check collects only park subjects (`_records(repo, "health_park:") == ["health_park:T1"]`) and the break check independently counts break events (`len(broke) == 1 and broke[0].data["broken_by"] == "ddflow:health"`); neither compares positions in the event log. Concretely, if the implementation expired/broke the lease first and parked agent-a afterwards, both lists still have exactly one matching entry, `st.items["T1"].lease.expired_at` is still set, and `(tree / "unfinished.py")` still reads "# nowhere else\n", so every assertion passes even though the safety property the rename asserts — parking the lane so its work is kept *before* the lease is broken — is violated. A regression that reverses park and break would therefore go undetected; the test should assert the park event's index precedes the break event's index in `EventLog(repo, "r").read_all()`.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_health_watch.py:194 (`test_mode_apply_parks_then_breaks_the_stalled_lease_and_keeps_its_work`)

chunk_findings.detail: The change deletes the only regression test that enforced the watchdog's destructive-action ban. The removed test read the source of the health/watchdog modules and asserted that none of `os.kill`, `killpg`, `rmtree`, `W.remove`, `unlink(` or `subprocess` appear anywhere in them, with the explicit comment that "the check above is the point". Nothing in the replacement tests reinstates that property: the new cases (`test_a_dead_harness_is_crashed_in_a_real_repo_and_apply_records_the_expiry`, `test_unresponsive_after_reply_s_parks_then_breaks_and_keeps_the_work`) assert only that a single sentinel file in one worktree survives one particular ladder step, and they now *import and call* `subprocess` in the test module itself rather than policing the product modules. Concretely: if the park/take-over/escalate path is later (or already) implemented with `shutil.rmtree(lease.worktree)` or `os.kill(pid, SIGKILL)` — exactly the destructive primitives the removed test forbade — every test in this file still passes, even though the intent states the ladder must "Never discards work, never acts on a lane with progress" and every step must be "reversible". The removal of this invariant is not compensated by any assertion in the diff, so the safety guarantee the watchdog is built around is now untested.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_health_watch.py (removed `test_the_watchdog_has_no_process_kill_or_delete_path`)

chunk_findings.detail: The scan's only exemption is `name == "kill"`, but signal 0 ("null signal") is the POSIX existence probe for every process-signalling API in `KILLERS`, not just `os.kill`. `os.killpg(pgid, 0)` (line 38 lists `killpg`) and `Popen.send_signal(0)` (listed as `send_signal`) end nothing — they only test whether the group/child exists — yet `_is_probe` returns False for them, so `test_every_process_signal_in_ddflow_is_on_a_child_it_started` reports them as "unreviewed process-signalling call(s)". Concrete failure: a liveness helper like `def alive(pgid): return os.killpg(pgid, 0) == 0` anywhere in `ddflow/` outside the six listed functions fails the suite even though the call cannot end a process, contradicting the test's own docstring ("every call that can end a process ... must be one of the sites below").
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_no_kill_paths.py:62-69 (`_is_probe`)

chunk_findings.detail: The `replace`/`move` carve-out only recognizes a *literal* receiver (`ast.Constant`/`ast.JoinedStr`), so `.replace(...)` on a string held in a variable, an attribute, or a concatenation is treated as a deletion in `test_the_watchdog_modules_signal_nothing_and_delete_nothing`. Concrete failure: `core/health.py` line `evidence = tpl.replace("{lane}", lane)` (or `msg = self.summary.replace(", ", ";")`) is appended to `bad` as `replace() in ...` although no file is touched, and `assert not bad` fails; the same over-match applies to `remove`/`move` on in-memory containers, e.g. `findings.remove(f)`, which get no exemption at all even though they delete no work. The exemption is thus incomplete for the very case it was written to cover.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_no_kill_paths.py:97 and 102-105 (`_is_str_call`)

chunk_findings.detail: The golden config registered here records the watchdog's global correction mode as `health.mode = 'propose'`. The watchdog interface it is supposed to render fixes this knob as `[watch].act = off | advise | act, default advise` (intent section 3; conformance r-everything-configurable). A project that follows the documented interface and sets the mode to the documented middle value `advise` is addressing a value that does not appear in the recorded knob space, and the shipped default `propose` is not one of the three documented ladder modes. The transcript is the golden rendering of the registered config, so either the default/value set must be `off | advise | act` with `advise`, or the spec's documented value set is wrong; as recorded, the two disagree.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_uc_surf_setup_ops_transcript.json (`health.mode = 'propose'`)

chunk_findings.detail: The change adds per-finding-kind mode overrides for exactly six of the watchdog's conditions — `health.mode_idle`, `health.mode_stalled`, `health.mode_unresponsive`, `health.mode_locked`, `health.mode_crashed`, `health.mode_runaway` — but no override for STARVED, even though STARVED is listed in section 1 as one of the conditions every lane must be inspected for ("STARVED = context or quota pressure from the governor"). Likewise there is no other `health.*` key covering starved lanes. Because the requirement is that "every limit, mode and interval [is] a knob settable by file, CLI, MCP and prompt, per project and org" and that the correction ladder's mode is set "per finding kind", a starved lane's step cannot be configured to off/advise/act at all. A `health.mode_starved = 'inherit'` entry is missing from the recorded default config.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_uc_surf_setup_ops_transcript.json (missing `health.mode_starved`)
